project_tracker_diagnostic: Woody-based or shrubby white composite with opposite leaves and clusters of discoid white heads; much more shrubby than herbaceous bonesets.

project_inclusion.learning_reason: Common or useful Central Texas fall/white composite for field learning.

morphology_keys.habit: Rounded shrubby plant, often woody at the base.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite, ovate to triangular-ovate, serrate, often aromatic when crushed.
morphology_keys.heads: Small white discoid heads in terminal corymbs or panicles.
morphology_keys.fna_confirmation: FNA: shrub 69–150 cm (rarely 30–200 cm), petioles 3–10(–15) mm, deltate to broadly ovate (sometimes hastate) leaves generally 3–5 × 2–5 cm; leaves essentially gland-free; involucres 4–6 mm; foliage persistent in the US flora.

look_here_first: First look for the woody shrubby base and persistent opposite sharply toothed broad leaves on short 3–10(–15) mm petioles. Then inspect an individual white to faint-pink head sideways: involucre 4–6 mm. Versus Chromolaena odorata, avoid color alone; its involucres are LONG CYLINDRICAL 8–10 mm with 4–6+ phyllary series.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Against A. altissima: persistent woody shrub structure and relatively short petioles versus rhizomatous herb with broader long-petioled leaves. Against Chromolaena odorata: 4–6 mm involucres, not 8–10 mm cylindrical heads with numerous layered phyllaries. Against E. serotinum: shrub rather than tall herbaceous branched perennial.
comparisons.caution: Single new green shoots may not betray the perennial woody base; compare mature stem base and whole plant.
